references.text: God warns that the heavens will become like iron and the earth like bronze, resulting in drought and lack of rain—a parallel curse for disobedience.
The Lord warns that He will shut up the heavens so there is no rain, and the land will not yield its produce—the same theme of withheld rain as punishment.
Elijah prophesies that there shall be neither dew nor rain over Israel—an fulfillment of the curse concerning withheld rain.
Solomon's prayer mentions that the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because of sin—a reference to the curse in Deuteronomy.
God withheld rain from Israel as punishment for their sin—a prophetic fulfillment of the curse.
Joel describes drought and devastation over the land as a judgment from God, consistent with the curses concerning withheld rain.
Haggai describes how God brought drought upon the land and all that grows—a judgment similar to the curse in Deuteronomy.
